title: From a 1:1: 'send lane-b a hello' → send_message, quiet confirm, reply relayed (no group post)

turns.prompt: Send lane-b a hello from me — just say hi and ask how its day is going.
turns.reply_regex_not: (?i)group|which chat|another chat|can't send|cannot send|couldn't send|only works

rubric.criteria: The agent messaged lane-b directly with its messaging tool from this 1:1 chat and told the user in one plain line that it was sent (for example 'Sent to lane-b.'). It did not ask which chat to use, did not propose posting in a group, and did not say it could not send. If lane-b's answer had already come back, relaying it in a line is fine.

turns.reply_regex_not: (?i)I can't check|no way to|not able to see

rubric.criteria: The agent relays lane-b's reply in one to three sentences (lane-b's own words or a faithful paraphrase), or says plainly that lane-b has not answered yet. It does not invent an answer and does not say it cannot know.

peer_lane_checks.note: For the runner (bc-dcc557ae): also dump lane-b's pinned chat. Expect one `role: project` row whose `sender` is `project:<lane-a id>` with `agentMessage.fromProjectId` = lane-a and `senderName` starting 'lane-a'; the assistant row answering it (inReplyTo = that row) carries `agentReplyTo` = lane-a's name. No new chat was created in either lane and no people-chat membership changed.

doc_checks.forbid_text_regex: only works inside a group|group-send|which chat|another chat|Projects ⇄

regression: agent-to-agent messaging (docs/agent-to-agent-messaging.md): hjkb → Doug hello from a 1:1, Oct 23; #1780 (one answer per question: check the relay inbox before saying nothing came back); run 15: #2303 — 'no reply yet' while the reply was already in the chat (fix in #2346)
